modal.helpHtml:
What it does

Combine interchangeable layer sets in a PSD (characters, clothes, expressions, text, and more) by rules, render each result, and package them as a ZIP. Compositing follows Photoshop's per-pixel behavior so exports match results made by toggling layers in Photoshop.

Five steps

  1. Layers: Select layers or groups that vary and make them an option group, or use “⇢ Children as options”.
  2. Groups: Choose a rule type and whether each group participates in combinations. Select an option to preview it.
  3. Rules: Add cross-group exclusions, conditional exclusions, absolute exclusions, or dependencies as needed.
  4. Combinations: Review every export; excluded combinations include a reason.
  5. Export: Choose a format and filename, then export a ZIP.

Rules at a glance

BehaviorWhereExample
Always shownGroup type “{fixedLabel}”{fixedExample}
Choose oneGroup type “{exclusiveLabel}”{exclusiveExample}
Choose one or noneGroup type “{optionalLabel}”{optionalExample}
Group exclusionExclusive and optional groups already allow at most one choicePut Chinese / English in one group
CombinationsParticipating groups are multipliedCharacter × clothes × expression
Cross-group exclusionRules page (whole groups)Chinese subtitles vs English subtitles
Conditional exclusionRules page (options)Character A cannot use outfit C
Absolute exclusionRules page (layers)Two layers never appear together
Multiple exclusionRules page, or select layers and choose exclusion on the Layers pageAt most one of several options across groups
DependencyRules pageChoosing eyelashes requires eyeliner

Two kinds of exclusion

Within a group: only one option can be selected, as defined by its type.
Across groups: different groups can conflict. Add a rule on the Rules page; invalid combinations are skipped with a reason on the Combinations page.

Common features

  • Node workflow: Open “Nodes” in the top bar. Drop a layer or folder onto a group to add one option, or onto empty space to create a group. “Split” turns folder children into separate options. Connect nodes to define combinations, exclusions, and dependencies.
  • Combination counts: Choose one multiplies by the option count, optional multiplies by count plus one, and multi-select multiplies by 2 to the option count. The node and Groups pages show each factor.
  • Clear / reset: Clear all groups on the Groups page or reset to the imported state on Export. Importing the same file again restores its previous settings.
  • Smart detection: The Layers page suggests groups from folder structure and names. Select suggestions to create them in one step.
  • Search: Enter a name at the top of Layers to show matching layers and their parent groups.
  • Show / hide: Click the eye beside a layer. Preview and export use the current visibility; you can restore the original state.
  • Atomic groups: Multi-layer parts can be shown as a unit. Expand one to control the visibility of its layers.
  • Export scope: Selected, all valid combinations, or all possible combinations ignoring exclusions.
  • Config files: Export settings to a config file and import them into another PSD.
  • Preview gestures: Drag to pan, pinch or use the wheel to zoom, rotate with two fingers or Shift+wheel, and double-click to reset.

Layers outside option groups

These appear in every export using the visibility saved in the PSD. Selecting an option automatically shows its parent groups.

Layer-name tags (psd-export CLI compatible)

[1] main tag; [jp@lang] option jp in group lang; [+logo] always shown; [#censor] ignored; [1:4] expands to 1 through 4. Tagged PSDs create option groups automatically on import.

Known limits

Adjustment layers, some layer effects, and vector masks are not rendered. Scaled pattern overlays may have subtle edge differences from Photoshop.

Settings are saved per file and restored the next time you open the same PSD.
